text: This is a common money mule recruitment tactic observed by the Police, which typically does not involve any real work, especially considering the high wages being offered.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For every money mule investigated, there are usually many more victims who will never recover their monies lost.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This must surely be considered when deciding whether or not to prosecute someone.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Murali suggested having a policy not to hold individuals criminally liable if they speedily report transactions to the Police, even if they might have been negligent in the first place.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The authorities will take this into account during investigations, though I will not go so far as to say that they should be automatically freed of criminal liability.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Each case has to be assessed on its own facts and circumstances.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Louis Ng asked about the "red flags" that individuals should watch out for.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: He and Mr Zhulkarnain also asked about the extent of verification needed to address suspicious behaviour.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It begins with having a clear understanding of our payment accounts, including our bank accounts, and Singpass.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: First, everyone must understand that these accounts are for our own use.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They should not be used by another person, especially if we do not know who the other party is or what the transactions are for.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Second, as a rule, we do not share details about these accounts because they should only be operated by ourselves.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: With this understanding in mind, the common tactics used by scammers to approach prospective victims become easier to recognise.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: One common tactic by scammers is not to present themselves in person.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Instead, they tend to connect out of the blue through phone calls or video calls, claiming to help you or to need help from you.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Can such a mysterious person be trusted with privileged information?

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Another common tactic is to give various fairly well-rehearsed reasons for you to let someone else use your account to receive or transfer monies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It should cause us to ask – why can this person not use their own account instead?

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It is also common for scammers to give reasons for wanting your bank account login or Singpass credentials.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But think a little bit – why should you hand over the keys to anyone to unlock your valuables?

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These "red flags" are by no means exhaustive, but they should set off alarm bells.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In general, my advice to the public is: if you are told something very bad has happened to you or your loved ones, pause and think.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Scammers love to make people panic because that is when we lose our best judgement.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: On the other hand, if you are told something that sounds too good to be true, also pause and think.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Scammers know that greed can make fools of geniuses.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Also, the bigger the amount at stake, the more carefully you should proceed.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To summarise, we would like everyone to be vigilant and take proper care of our payment accounts and Singpass accounts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Police and the AGC will act judiciously.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Sharael Taha asked whether platforms such as Apple Pay and Google Pay are included in the amendments to the CDSA (Amendment) Bill.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It is a good question because the money mules do not only use traditional banking accounts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: On Singpass abuse, Mr Sharael asked how prevalent the problem is and whether individuals selling or inadvertently giving their Singpass credentials to scammers were aware of the implications.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: While the large majority of money mule cases involved abuse of bank accounts, the Police has observed a worrying trend of Singpass abuse.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I spoke about the challenges to prove wrongful intent when trying to prosecute offending Singpass users.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We have seen cases where the user is taught by scammers how he can lie to the Police to get himself off the hook.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As Dr Tan Wu Meng reminded us during Question Time yesterday, we cannot be fighting yesterday's war only, but must be ready to tackle new scam tactics as they evolve.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Having seen such behaviours with Singpass, I seek Members' support to empower the Police to arrest a likely trend and not wait till cases have snowballed.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Sharael also asked whether the proposed penalties in the CMA (Amendment) Bill are sufficient.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will monitor the situation after the offences come into effect and see whether adjustments are needed, including to deal with other forms of cybercrime, which is also something that Ms Janet Ang mentioned.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Ms Lim asked whether prosecution rates of money mules will increase with the new offences.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Ms Ang also raised questions about the enforcement of the new laws, including the challenges relating to the transnational nature of the scam syndicates.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: However, both Bills are also intended to clearly set the guardrails for the proper use of payment accounts and Singpass accounts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But, like Ms Lim, I will not be so sanguine.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We must remain vigilant and be ready to up the ante, if needed.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For cases involving offences committed overseas, we will work with our international counterparts, though I am sure Members are familiar with some of the challenges of overseas enforcement.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I also fully agree with Mr Sharael, Ms Ang, Ms Yeo and Mr Zhulkarnain on the need to educate the public.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will cooperate with key stakeholders and intensify public education efforts before implementing the Bills to explain the dangers, the new guard rails and the "red flags" that we should be mindful of.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Louis Ng spoke about section 8B(4) of the CMA Bill, which states that the mere transmission of Singpass credentials by network access providers and data transmission service providers does not amount to an offence under the new section 8B.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For avoidance of doubt, section 8B(4) makes clear that service providers, such as telecommunication companies (telcos), will not have committed an offence merely because their networks or services were used as the conduit or platform for the transmission of credentials.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is because it would neither be fair nor reasonable in these circumstances to expect such providers to know whether a person was using their networks or services to transmit the credentials of another person.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Ng asked about the responsibility of these providers in addressing the illegal use of bank accounts and Singpass credentials.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The bigger question is how they can help prevent scams from taking place.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I have spoken previously about our efforts in this area, including the Infocomm Media Development Authority's work with the telcos to block spoofed calls and SMSes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We are also working with the telcos to block suspicious websites in a speedier fashion.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: On Mr Yip's comment that the CMA Bill may be contrary to the general position of "innocence until proven guilty", let me assure Members that this is not so.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The presumption of innocence is a fundamental principle, and in fact the foundation of our criminal justice system.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In both Bills, the overall burden remains on the Prosecution to prove the offences beyond reasonable doubt.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Next, I will deal with the questions and suggestions which relate to our broader anti-scam efforts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I will do so briefly because these fall outside the scope of the Bills and some of them have been discussed in this House before.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We have taken proactive measures to: educate the public; prevent and block scammers from being able to reach victims in the first place; make it easier to detect and report scams; and enforce and recover lost monies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I have given some examples in my opening speech, which address Mr Yip, Ms Ang and Mr Sharael's questions about our efforts in these areas.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will step up our efforts, including enabling our Police with technology like Mr Sharael suggested.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In line with Ms Yeo's suggestion, we will continue to work with relevant Government agencies like MAS and the banks to provide assistance to scam victims, and also leverage analytics to detect and mitigate scam-related transactions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In line with Mr Murali's suggestion, we will also continue to work with parties which rely on Singpass to do more to prevent scams.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Yip and Ms Ang asked about Singpass security.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Smart Nation and Digital Government Group has introduced the following measures to better protect Singpass users.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: GovTech has put in place early detection mechanisms and fraud analytics to detect potential scams involving Singpass.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is a useful feature because most scammers operate outside of Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: So, if you block your Singpass from overseas access, in essence, you are preventing it from being abused by overseas scammers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Some of these measures can also help to protect the more vulnerable members of our society, which Mr Zhulkarnain had asked about.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: GovTech and the Police will study how best to implement them.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Everyone has a role to play in the fight against scams and should exercise care and responsibility in the use of our payment accounts and Singpass.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Scammers are not remaining static and neither can we.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will continue to conduct regular security reviews and enhance our defences.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Even as we prepare to respond to future threats, I am glad that Members agree on the need for these Bills to tackle the pressing issues at hand.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I note the hon Second Minister's response to my suggestion about not holding persons criminally liable in the event that they lodge a Police report of monies that they have received in their accounts.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I would just like to clarify that what my proposal is, is actually in the context of persons who were negligent in having their accounts being used and subsequently realised when the monies came in, that their accounts were misused, and therefore they proceed to lodge a Police report.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Certainly not advocating a carte blanche to deal with all scenarios.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: On the Member's second question which has to do with due diligence, he had referred to the actions that landlords can take under the Immigration Act to, in some sense, demonstrate that they have done their part in trying to prevent illicit activities.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But as many Members have noticed and commented on during their speeches, the scam types and tactics are evolving so quickly.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In fact, the measures that we have to take to protect ourselves are still a matter that is evolving each day.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As the scam types present themselves, we notice increasingly new actions that we will have to take to protect ourselves and to protect our accounts from being misused.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, appreciating the Member's very well-intended suggestions, we would certainly like to get to a point where we can articulate "here are the three things or five things that you can do".
